articleTitle: Two-dimensional graphic visualization of objects using distance measurement with ultrasonic waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The measurement process of the echo arrival time of an ultrasonic wave allows to determine the distance to an object or surface and to graph the objects present in the environment from the position of the ultrasonic transducer. In this work, a system with two bipolar stepper motors is developed, the first for the linear displacement of a 40 KHz ultrasonic transducer and the second for the rotation of the transducer. With the value of the displacement, the angle of rotation and the distance to the objects, polar coordinates are used to visualize the environment in two dimensions in a graphical interface. To calculate the propagation speed of the ultrasonic waves, the ambient temperature is considered. The test surfaces are flat and horizontal.

articleTitle: Development of a training system for gross psychomotor skills in visually impaired individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Individuals who are affected with partial or total vision loss, deal with great difficulties in their daily lives. Among them, a particular challenge is the psychomotor development being hindered due to the impossibility of gathering psychomotor information through vision to replicate it.Thus, this project presents a training system that assists in the development of gross psychomotor skills using haptic technologies applied to a modular suit, which is adaptable to most types of bodies and replicable. A web interface was created to interpret and plot data, helping to observe where further assistance is required for the improvement of the patients’ gross psychomotor system. With the help of the Topos Puebla FC team for the blind, the necessary tests were carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the system, measuring and comparing reference angles with the control model during several exercise routines, obtaining the necessary data to observe the user's performance, and gathering the user’s feedback about the system for further improvements.This project is a breakthrough in the integration of hardware and software for medical applications, providing real-time physical feedback during motor development activities. The positive feedback from end users supports the user-centered orientation and continuous improvement of the system, enabling a better quality of life for people with special needs in the future.

articleTitle: Design and construction of a smart support system for the visually impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This project implements ultrasonic sensors in a visual device to detect objects at close distances that serves as support for people with visual disabilities, thus supporting the inclusion in society of these people and thus preventing future accidents, the main idea of the project is to have this device at a low cost so that it can be accessible to as many people as possible and support in achieving independence.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the use of wooden pallets to modify the thermal envelope as a solution to reduce temperature in the CJR Company Office
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Thermal comfort inside residential buildings is already a permanent need that today is resolved through the use of air conditioning systems. Most of these devices consume a high level of electrical energy, which is why they have become a energy service of important weight in the electricity demand of the residential, commercial and industrial sector in Mexico, with its imminent impact on the infrastructure of the SEN (National Electric System). An alternative solution to reduce consumption due to air conditioning is thermal envelopes, these are implemented in the construction of the building; However, there are existing buildings that did not take this type of solution into account, so conditioning the existing thermal envelope is the best option. This article presents, through the use of software, how the use of pallets can contribute to improving the cooling conditions of the roof of a particular home.

articleTitle: Development of a layout with CMOS tecnology for the red blood cell measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In our country, chronic-degenerative diseases such as diabetes and high blood pressure have increased and are one of the main causes of death in the world where cerebral infarctions and myocardial attacks are increasingly common. These diseases can be caused by factors such as stress, tobacco or alcohol use, high cholesterol, genetics, blood pressure and diabetes. The latter can be caused by changes in lifestyle and diet, especially in low-income areas where processed foods high in sugar, carbohydrates and fats are more accessible. For this reason, it is important to have early detection systems in the health system to control these diseases and increase the life expectancy of patients but with the help of the CMOS technology together with a microfluidic sensor can help detect these diseases early through its microchannels.

articleTitle: Strategy for the Evaluation and Selection of Innovative Technological Projects in Public Universities of México
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Nowadays, the importance of a country's ability to transform knowledge into technology is undeniable. The industry as a whole has ceased to have exclusivity as the creator of technological innovation. Although the industry remains a significant source of innovation today, the production of technological innovation has extended to the "Edge of the source of knowledge" (universities and research centers). As a result of the pressure on universities to contribute to society beyond research and education, innovation and technology transfer have emerged as a third mission. All this is based on the certainty that universities have the capacity to generate knowledge and develop technology. Unlike the generation of knowledge, where we have extensive experience, the technology developed in universities is "Basic Academic Technology," which makes it difficult to transfer. In other words, it follows the same pattern used in basic research development. In this work, we present an initial analysis for the creation of a reference model for Institutional Technology Development in public universities in Mexico, taking our experience at IPN as a reference case. Our model is based on the hypothesis that the conditions for technological development in public institutions are similar: no technological foresight studies, scarce or no economic resources, immediate expected results, complex regulatory processes for technology transfer, and few incentives for developers. Our model separates the processes with institutional funding for research development from the processes for technological development. The evaluation of technological projects, unlike research projects, should primarily assess the maturity of the proposed project rather than the academic trajectory of the proposer. The proposed model aims to create processes that promote mature technological development with the necessary characteristics for transfer.

articleTitle: Neonicotinoids Interaction with CuO Clusters: A DFT Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The interaction between Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> clusters with the neonicotinoid pesticides Acetamiprid, Thiacloprid and Thiamethoxam is studied using the energy of the boundary orbitals (HOMO-LUMO) and electron density. In pesticide molecules, a specific distribution of loads is observed in the functional groups, giving rise to areas of high reactivity. Interaction with pesticides reduces the calculated band gap in clusters, i.e. from 1.19 eV until 1.13 eV for Cu6O6 and from 1.37 eV until 1.11 eV for Cu12O12. Adsorption energies (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ads</inf>) and Gibbs free energies (Deltha G) show a strong and exergonic interactions, with Cu6O6 being more favorable with Thiacloprid (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ads</inf> -57.07 and Deltha G -34.39 kcal/mol) and less favorable for Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> with Thiamethoxam (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ads</inf> -29.36 and Deltha G -9.48 kcal/mol). These results are useful for the development of efficient and sustainable sensors based on semiconductor materials.

articleTitle: Real-time geolocation system for cargo transportation in the state of Hidalgo, with communication redundancy (LoRa and WiFi)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The present prototype based on the IOT architecture is presented as an innovative proposal for the solution of cargo transport theft since it proposes a real-time monitoring system, there are several prototypes of this type but this one proposes a redundancy in the communication between LoRa and Wi-Fi since by only one using one of them the communication is exposed to be lost at some point and the transport is left vulnerable, in addition the prototype uses the GPS-Neo6m module and a humidity and temperature sensor that will allow monitoring of the load status

articleTitle: Identification Based Hammerstein-Wiener Neural Network for Propeller Pendulum PID control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work focuses on the design of a PID controller for a propeller pendulum system based on the approximation of a transfer function using a Hammerstein-Wiener neural network (H-W NN). The identification process is performed by obtaining experimental data and the H-W NN model is presented with a reduction approach without loss of accuracy and computational cost under a reduction method. Subsequently, a transfer function based on approximations with the H-W NN is proposed and the Matlab PID tuner is used to obtain the controller values. The experimental data of the PID controller applied to the propeller pendulum and the simulation data are shown.

articleTitle: Remote Control and Automation of UR3 Robot with IoT and Vision Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work investigates the integration of the UR3 robot from Universal Robots and MATLAB using IoT technology. The proposal involves implementing a vision algorithm in MATLAB to detect an operator's arm movements and utilizing a cloud service platform to transmit the instructions remotely to an industrial network that will assign the UR3 robot a predefined routine. Key components for this technological integration include the Siemens S7-1500 PLC, ESP32 and Adafruit microcontrollers, Node-Red software, and the AWS platform. This project demonstrates the effective integration of various technologies and platforms, offering a robust and flexible solution for the remote control and automation of robotic systems.

articleTitle: Relationship of optical techniques in the carotenoid content in mango
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: It is essential to preserve food for longer; one way to maintain it is through dehydration and the appropriate pretreatments to protect its properties. In the case of mango, it is a product that reaches many families, so in this work, mango without pretreatment (STT), mango with pretreatment with ascorbic acid (TAA), and pretreatment with osmotic dehydration (ODT) were compared. By Raman spectroscopy and absorbance, the pretreatment that favored the conservation of the β-carotene content was qualitatively determined. This is a very important property for various applications. Samples with TAA were found to retain the highest amount of the aforementioned compound.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Maximum Temperature in a Locality of the Coastal Area of the Gulf of Mexico in the Thermoperivallon, from 1981 to 2021
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Regression analysis, ANOVA, Tukey's test and statistical models of the behavior of the meteorological variable Maximum Temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>) in the range from May 1 to October 31 (thermoperivallon) from 1981 to 2021 were performed. Being able to compare the results of These analyzes with the graphic results could provide a clearer vision of the historical behavior of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> at the local level in the Veracruz-Boca del Río Conurbation Zone (ZCVB) and the forecast of its future behavior, being a requirement for care. of living beings in this ecosystem. This deep and detailed analysis allows us to find that the behavior pattern of the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> variable presents a positive slope, which shows maximum temperatures equal to or greater than 31 °C from the year 2009 and continues upward until the end of the year. period analyzed (2021). The regression analysis with its corresponding residuals, allowed us to observe a forecast with also ascending characteristics of the maximum temperatures. Therefore, it can be affirmed that the graphic analysis and the mathematical analysis of the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> variable is reliable to determine the constant and continuous increase of this in the ZCVB. Finally, the probability of observing temperatures higher than 31 °C is 0.5618.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Ag nanodendrites via Galvanic replacement and Laser-assisted reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Dendritic silver structures were produced via Galvanic replacement and Laser assisted reduction. The dendrites speed formation and growth were determined by electron scanning microscope. Results show an increased structure formation for the laser-assisted process due to chemical activation of Ag ions by UV irradiation. Obtained chemical compound were observed by Raman spectroscopy. As it is shown, Ag nanodendrites tends to react to carbon compound present in environment leaving traces of some carbonate substance on the substrate surface. The present work give an insight of structural evolution and stability of Ag nanodendrites related to the structural characteristics of the substrates used.

articleTitle: Offline Parameter Identification of Second-order Discrete Systems using Metaheuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The analysis of dynamic systems is essential in the design of both classical and modern controllers, especially in situations where obtaining accurate model parameters is complex. This difficulty stems from the uncertain and variable nature of many real systems, which can compromise the effectiveness of the designed controllers. In order to address this problem, this article proposes developing an innovative methodology based on the Rooted Tree Optimization (RTO) algorithm. This algorithm, inspired by the natural behavior of plant roots moving toward the nearest water sources, is used as a metaphor for the search for optimal parameters. In particular, the methodology suggests the optimization of the parameters of the discrete transfer function of second-order systems, thus seeking to improve the accuracy and robustness of the dynamic models used in control. In addition, tests were carried out where the signal measurement was contaminated by random noise to obtain the model parameters, showing robustness in searching for parameters, even when the signal was unclear.

articleTitle: Detection, measurement, and segmentation of aluminum profiles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This project addresses the need for computerized inspection of aluminum profiles in a manufacturing cell. For inventory management, it is necessary to automate the classification and measurement of the aluminum profile. The manufacturing cell's proposed configuration strategically positions two cameras and implements a YOLOv8 convolutional neural network for precise and rapid part identification. An online database is implemented for accurate stock management.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Electro-Optical Prototype Real-Time Water Qualitative Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work presents the design and development of an electro-optical prototype real-time water qualitative monitoring system. This prototype is based on using a red Light-Emitting Diode (LED, wavelength of 650 nm) as the incident light and a monolithic photodiode (OPT101). The water to be analyzed is placed in a laboratory test tube between the path of the emitted light and the photodiode. Depending on the type of water, the OPT110 delivers a particular voltage level. Thus, it is possible to determine qualitatively the quality of the water. Potentially, the obtained result of this proposal can be extended to the analysis of other liquids such as alcoholic drinks.

articleTitle: Monitoring agricultural irrigation canals with LoRa and Zabbix technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Currently, irrigation canal systems face numerous problems that could be avoided with timely monitoring and detection. Our Internet of Things (IoT) prototype aims to monitor these irrigation lines using advanced technologies, such as LoRa (IEEE 802.15.4a), for long-distance communication and low energy consumption. Additionally, the use of the open-source monitoring system Zabbix is highlighted for reading and visualizing metrics based on the NOM-001-SEMARNAT-2021 regulation of Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (SEMARNAT).The collected data, including pH, turbidity, and temperature, will be sent in full through a Gateway. This Gateway will receive the data and transmit it via MQTT to the server in JSON format. In this way, we can detect anomalies in real-time and alert the corresponding authorities promptly.

articleTitle: Development of an Object Recognition-Based Assistance System for Surgical Instrumentation Using an UR5e Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Given the critical shortage of surgical instrument nurses, especially in Mexico, with a deficit of 68.9%, this study presents the development of a prototype assisted by artificial intelligence to enhance efficiency and safety in low-risk surgical procedures. The prototype utilizes object recognition to assist in surgical instrumentation. The methodology includes creating a dataset of images representing surgical instruments, using YOLOv8 for object identification, MediaPipe for detecting key points in the hands, and setting up a visual space using an Intel RealSense camera. These data are transformed into Cartesian coordinates to communicate with a UR5 collaborative robot using Python. The surgical instruments identified with YOLOv8 were classified into five categories: scalpel, forceps, curved Mayo scissors, straight Mayo scissors, and a discriminative class. The use of the pre-trained MediaPipe model allowed the system to identify handoff points for the instruments on the surgeon's hand. Additionally, the Intel RealSense depth camera facilitates the calculation of the viewing area size, enabling the determination of specific coordinates for the UR5 robot, which uses the key points generated by YOLOv8 and MediaPipe. This prototype provides a comprehensive solution to address the shortage of surgical instrument nurses in surgical settings, promoting closer and more effective collaboration between medical professionals and advanced technology.

articleTitle: Reduction in electronic components for an fNIRS system for monitoring cerebral hemodynamic activity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In certain cases, it is necessary to use several sensors that record a certain event or situation that is occurring in the control plant. Such as medical instruments whose sensors are placed in different areas of the patient's body, either recording electrical activity of the heart (electrocardiogram) or the brain (electroencephalograph). One of these cases is near-infrared spectroscopy systems (fNIRS), which require a substantially high number of sensors that record the hemodynamic activity of the cerebral cortex by means of photodiodes placed in different areas of the scalp.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation of Water Droplets on Plant Leaves for Sustainable Energy Harvesting in Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Droplet interactions with surfaces are a common phenomenon in nature and have a wide range of applications in agriculture and industry. These include on-farm disinfection, surface coating, and power transmission. Previous research has primarily focused on deposition, the bouncing behavior of droplets upon impacting stationary leaves, and the mechanical modeling and motion behavior of leaves under droplet load. However, the relationship between contact electrification (CE) and motion behavior during droplet impact on leaf surfaces remains a case study. This study investigates the interaction between electrification and motion behavior when a droplet impacts a living leaf surface as it courses. These results were close to the first studies of the experimental evaluation in the laboratory, which was 320 mV, evaluated by Maxwell's law and c compared to the evaluation performed by COMSOL, which solves by Gauss's law obtaining 0.311 mV. However, it is related to what was obtained in the experimental test.

articleTitle: Design and Construction of Ethylene Vinyl Acetate Beveling Machine for the Footwear Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Develop and test of a bevel machine for innersoles of ethyl-vinyl-acetate layer for shoe fabrication. Design of the machine's principal component, the shaft, done to support the loads after a meticulous calculation and analysis. Implementation of an ergonomic study to ensure the comfort and efficiency of the workers using the machine. The potential impact of this machine on the footwear industry is significant, promising improved production processes and workers conditions.

articleTitle: How machine learning-based competitiveness indexes analysis may help us become a wealthy nation with improved living standards: case study Mexico
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work we analyze the competitiveness data of the IMCO (Mexican Institute for competitiveness) 2003-2022, the ten different subindexes provide us with an overview of the evolution and performance of the Mexican nation. By using machine learning techniques, we examine the subindexes (indicators) that most significantly affect the overall competitiveness score. Once these indicators have been identified, simulations are performed to obtain 6-years projections. Two scenarios are accounted: in the first, nothing is done and the future is simply predicted based on the status quo. In the latter, however, certain actions are applied to the previously determined indicators in order to enhance them. Lastly, suggestions are made in accordance with the estimates found from the scenario simulation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Wear on Copper Pipes Deposited in Different Environments: An Understanding of Damage in Geothermal Heat Exchangers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This study presents the evaluation and comparison of damage in samples of commercial copper pipes exposed to different environments: atmospheric conditions, underground, seawater, and river water. These environments were selected to contrast the alterations in outer diameter and thickness that pipes used in geothermal heat exchangers may undergo. The exposure period for the samples was 155 days, with results measured experimentally and analyzed statistically. The findings indicate that the samples exposed to seawater and underground conditions exhibit the greatest reductions in outer diameter and thickness, respectively, while the sample exposed to atmospheric conditions does not show a significant damage rate.

articleTitle: Study of perception on the use of generative artificial intelligence in higher-level students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools are advanced systems capable of generating content in formats such as text, images, or videos, which has been transforming fields such as education. However, excessive use of these tools may result in students not fully utilizing their own skills, thereby diminishing their critical thinking, analytical abilities, and information search skills. This research aims to study the perceptions of higher education students regarding GAI tools to assess their experiences with the usefulness of these instruments and their impact on learning. To achieve this, a non-experimental, comparative, descriptive research approach with a quantitative focus was employed, involving theoretical and conceptual processing. An instrument was designed to measure dimensions such as ethics, experience, usefulness, and quality. Finally, the results revealed that students use and understand basic concepts of GAI tools, recognize their limitations, and are thus familiar with them. The study also identified certain risks related to students' perception of these tools as substitutes for their teachers rather than as supportive aids and noted that they are perceived as potentially diminishing students' learning capacity.

articleTitle: IoT monitoring and control prototype with Zabbix and LoRa communication, for Tilapia Biofloc systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work, a monitoring prototype is made for the treatment of tilapia farming through sensors and the use of actuators to control the physicochemical parameters of the water, using the Zabbix platform for the visualization of the key variables, in addition to the use of the LoRa communication protocol, all under the Internet of Things environment, to have a set of nodes and carry out better control in a biofloc farming farm. A study is carried out on the LoRa technology applicable to IoT environments in different devices and development boards. The technologies are chosen, and the user interface design is configured on an opensource platform called Zabbix that allows the visualization of the data received by the IoT prototype. Finally, the Hardware is developed with an ESP32 development board with LoRa included from the Heltec brand and temperature sensors (DS18B0), PH (PH-4502C), DTS (Analog TDS Meter) and oxygen along with the software that is responsible for the data emission with Zabbix. During the tests of the work it is concluded that the prototype with sensors meets the objectives proposed in this work.

articleTitle: Dynamic model based control for trajectory following for an inspection-class ROV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This article is centered on the trajectory control of an inspection class remotely operated vehicle (ROV) based on a 5-thruster configuration generating four degrees of freedom (dof), three longitudinal movements and one rotation onto its yaw. The implemented control is a model-based strategy, and as a way of having redundant measurement, a velocity observer was designed. The validation is done under numerical simulation based on Runge-Kutta solver via Matlab. The graphic results show the effectiveness of the control and observer proposed.

articleTitle: Apparent Power Analysis in Transformers of the Faculty of Engineering: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this study, we evaluated the energy efficiency of two electrical transformers from the Faculty of Engineering of the Universidad Veracruzana. Through precise voltage and current measurements, we determine the apparent power of each piece of equipment and compare it to its rated capacity. The results reveal that while one transformer operates close to its optimal capacity, the other presents significant underutilization. This disparity in performance suggests the need for more efficient management of electrical load in the faculty. By analyzing the data obtained, we identified clear opportunities to enhance the use of these strategic devices. We propose a number of measures, such as regular audits, implementation of monitoring systems, and possible resizing, to ensure that transformers operate efficiently and reliably. By optimizing the use of these ones, not only energy costs are reduced, but also their useful life is prolonged, contributing to the sustainability of the institution electrical infrastructure.

articleTitle: Educational HIL-Based Testing System for DC-DC Power Converter Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and implementation of reliable and cost-effective testing equipment based on Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) for evaluating and validating DC-DC power converter control systems, focusing on educational applications. HIL simulation provides significant advantages over traditional simulation methods by enabling rapid and safe testing of converter topologies under conditions that closely resemble actual operation given good mathematical modeling of the physical system. This system supports the monitoring and control of power converters, making it highly suitable for enhancing practical learning and training in educational environments. Utilizing LabVIEW and CompactRIO hardware, the developed HIL test equipment is fully customizable to the parameters of various DC-DC circuits, facilitating the design process and providing a hands-on learning experience. The results demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed HIL system, offering a robust and accessible solution to the challenges of existing commercial and customized HIL approaches in academic settings.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Generative Language Tools for Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The development of technology has marked great changes in all areas, especially in education, the incorporation of various tools supported by artificial intelligence has brought positive and negative consequences, in many cases there is a lack of knowledge of these and therefore they have not been properly used. This study attempts to evaluate and compare some generative language tools through a literature search and their practical use. Using content analysis, the seven selected tools were compared considering the criteria of: Efficiency, Quality, Usability, Scalability and Costs. The results show that tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Whisper, Hugging Face and Grammarly stand out for their high efficiency, quality, usability and scalability, being the most robust options for various educational applications. While tools such as Google Bard and Khan Academy's AI Tutor offer good evaluations in usability and scalability, with relatively low costs, making them accessible and effective in educational environments. Some limitations were identified in tools such as Talk to Books and ChatPDF that present challenges in efficiency and usability, limiting their applicability compared to more advanced tools. In addition, GPT for Slides, although functional for presentations, shows limitations in scalability and security. It was identified that there is a positive correlation between efficiency and quality in most tools, although there are exceptions where these aspects are not aligned. It is concluded that generative tools in Higher Education are crucial to modernize teaching and are aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Choosing the right tool should consider factors such as security, costs and ease of use to maximize its educational impact.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an OTA for ECG Signals with High PSRR and CMRR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a high-gain, two-stage OTA. Using a 180 nm standard CMOS technology and resistive approximation techniques. The proposed symmetrical OTA, designed to function in the strong inversion region, achieves a gain of 72.06 dB, PSRR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, PSRR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> of 108 dB and 114 dB respectively, CMRR of 95 dB and a bandwidth of 22.9 kHz. Additionally, an IRN of 0.93 µVrms is obtained. Simulation results indicate that the designed OTA is a highly suitable candidate for biomedical applications, particularly for the detection and monitoring of electrocardiographic (ECG) signals.

articleTitle: Stability of a platform support vessel with a crawler crane on its main deck
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Supply and support vessels in the oil industry have stood out for their operational capabilities and their ease of structural adaptations to operational requirements. This article presents the evaluation of the static stability of a supply and support vessel, where it is proposed to install a 103-ton crawler crane because it will perform maintenance operations offshore. This static stability analysis incorporates loads using finite element method (FEM) models. Four main boom lifting capacities are analysed (33.1 for a 16-meter boom length, 32.8 tons for a 19-meter boom length, 31.3 tons for a 34-meter boom length, and 22.1 tons for a 52-meter boom length). The results show that the ship has a stability reserve to maintain the angles of heel and trim below the 5° and 3° indicated by the regulatory regulations of ships.

articleTitle: Improvement Acid Pretreatment of Corn Stover for Efficient Pentose Production
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Pentoses are five-carbon sugars derived from various raw materials. They are increasingly important because they are used to produce high-value products such as xylitol, a highly sought-after sweetener known for its significant sweetness, which is utilized in various oral care products and foods.This study investigates the extraction of pentoses, specifically xylose from corn stover by employing a central composite design, and response surface methodology. The aim is to identify the optimal pretreatment conditions by evaluating the concentration of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (% v/v), pretreatment time (min), and Liquid-Solid Ratio (LSR) (mL/g), ultimately achieving xylose yields of up to 31.93 g/L.

articleTitle: Sound wave equations description and formulation with Finite Difference in Time Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The main objective of the present work is to show the development of acoustic pressure wave equations using the method of finite differences in the time domain. This work develops step by step the composition and parts that make up the acoustic pressure equations, this with the intention of simulating acoustic phenomena with precision.

articleTitle: Low Temperature Measurements and Methodology to Characterize NbTi Superconducting Wires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Superconducting materials, such as NbTi, are pivotal for numerous advanced technological applications, including quantum computing and radio-millimeter-wavelength astronomy, due to their ability to maintain signal integrity with zero resistance and minimal electrical noise, superconductor materials require cryogenic environments to function effectively. On this way, this research focuses on the methodology and experimental setup for studying the performance of a NbTi wire as an electrical conductor across different temperature stages on a newly designed sample holder within a pulse tube cooler. By investigating NbTi's superconducting properties and thermal conductivity under these conditions, we aim to optimize its use, thereby enhancing its application in precision instruments.

articleTitle: PD/PID Delayed Control of a Scalar Neutral System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work proposes the stabilization and control of a scalar neutral system through a delayed PD/PID controller, presenting the necessary and sufficient conditions to ensure the stability of the system. In addition, the stabilizing parameters that delimit the regions of stability are determined through a frequency analysis of the system. The performance of the proposal will be evaluated using a numerical example.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Traditional and Metaverse-Based Learning on Financial Decision-Making Skills in Mathematics Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of traditional versus metaverse-based learning methods in enhancing financial decision-making skills among mathematics students at Tecnológico de Monterrey. A total of 28 students were divided into control and experimental groups. Initially, both groups were tasked with evaluating the financial feasibility of acquiring a car, with the control group scoring an average of 85.5 and the experimental group scoring 83.79. For the second case study, the control group used traditional study methods, while the experimental group utilized metaverse-based learning resources. The control group scored an average of 89.64, while the experimental group scored 91.36. Paired t-tests revealed statistically significant improvements in both groups, with t-values of -3.41 (p = 0.0047) for the experimental group and -5.84 (p < 0.0001) for the control group. Feedback indicated traditional methods were perceived as monotonous and tiring, whereas metaverse-based learning was engaging and enjoyable. Post-intervention surveys highlighted the positive impact of metaverse-based learning on student engagement and comprehension. The findings suggest that immersive technologies like the metaverse can significantly enhance learning experiences and outcomes in financial mathematics education.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Maximum Temperature in a Locality of the Coastal Area of the Gulf of Mexico during the Cold front Season From 1981 To 2021
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The behavior of the meteorological variable Maximum Temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>) was analyzed by regression analysis, ANOVA, Tukey's test and statistical models, in the range of values from January 1 to April 30 and from November 01 to December 31 of the time period from 1981 to 2021. Being able to compare the results of these analyses with the visual results presented by the graphs for the daily use of human beings, could provide a clearer vision of the historical behavior of the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> at the local level in the Veracruz-Boca del Río Conurbation Zone (ZCVB) and the forecast of its future behavior. Therefore, a mathematical and statistical analysis is presented, together with the graphic support that allows to determine the behavior of this variable. This analysis allows us to find that the behavior pattern of the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> variable presents a positive trend and although it does not reach the value of 30°C towards the end of the analyzed period (2021), it does show a behavior that shows that this limit will be reached in the not-too-distant future. The regression analysis with its corresponding residuals, allowed us to observe a forecast with also ascending characteristics and a positive trend of the slope. Therefore, it can be said that the graphical analysis and mathematical analysis of the variable T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> is reliable to determine the constant and continuous increase of this in the ZCVB.

articleTitle: Optimizing BLDC Motor Design: Practical Insights and Decision Tree Methodology for Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motors are essential for their efficiency and performance across various applications. Optimizing their design involves analyzing parameters such as lamination stack length, air gap, slot depth, insulation, slot number, and slot opening. This study uses Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Steady State D-Q analysis with MOTORXP software to evaluate these parameters’ impacts on flux distribution, torque, and efficiency. The paper proposes a comprehensive empirical evaluation framework and a decision tree methodology for optimizing BLDC motor designs. These contributions offer detailed parameter analysis, systematic evaluation, and practical insights, enhancing motor design for improved performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance of Satellite Internet via PLC and Solar Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Solar panels represent a significant advancement in renewable energy, providing a sustainable and eco-friendly power source. It offers a clean and abundant alternative to fossil fuels, reducing carbon emissions and mitigating environmental impact. By converting sunlight into electricity through photovoltaic cells, solar panels enable communities to access reliable energy while minimizing dependence on finite resources. Similarly, satellite internet, such as that provided by projects like Starlink, offers a transformative means to deliver broadband connectivity to communities where traditional infrastructure is lacking. Using low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink aims to provide high-speed internet access to even the most remote and underserved regions, bridging the digital divide and empowering communities with access to educational, economic, and communication opportunities. The study aims to assess the feasibility of using satellite internet through Power Line Communication (PLC) in a renewable energy environment. By examining the impact of noise on data transmission in a solar-powered context, the research identifies the efficiency and reliability of PLC networks under these conditions.

articleTitle: Using Graph Theory on its Full Extent to Speed-up the Analysis of Resistive Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Resistive grids have been widely used in diverse applications such as electronic circuits, robotics, image processing and electrical energy networks. The analyses of these types of grids have been carried out by using brute-force methods that rely on nowadays computer power for achieving massive numerical calculations. This work introduces an analysis methodology that rests on basic concepts of Graph Theory in order to determine the values of the electrical variables of the resistive grid, namely nodal voltages and branch currents. As a main result, the topology of the grid is used on its full extent to achieve the task of analysis.

articleTitle: Electronic and Optical Characteristics of alfa and delta Bi2O3: A DFT Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the structural, electronic, and optical properties of alfa - Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and delta - Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> for optical sensing applications. The computations used density functional theory through CASTEP, which utilized the GGA correlational function and ultrasoft pseudo potential PBE. The resulting structural parameters align with the available theoretical and experimental evidence. The band structure of the two polymorphs was determined, alfa - Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> exhibiting an indirect band gap of 2.47 eV and delta - Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> exhibiting a direct band gap of 1.91 eV, respectively, in agreement with experimental data and theoretical findings. The hybridization of O-2p and Bi-6s orbitals was shown by the TDOS calculations and the PDOS of the Bi and O atoms. Both undergo optical absorption in the ultraviolet and a short range of visible light regions. The refractive index of both materials is comparable; this significant result arouses interest in studying the effects on oxygen absorption caused by the crystalline structure of the delta phase. The results of the optical conductivity reflect its semiconductor character, thereby validating the calculations obtained.

articleTitle: Detection of MB with Au-Ag nanostars on Cu foil and Cu(OH)2 nanowires substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work, several solutions were made with different concentrations of gold (Au), silver (Ag), observing considerable changes in the absorption spectra. In the absorption analysis of these samples, the characteristic spectrum of each of them was found, thus discovering the presence of nanostars, these were deposited on two different substrates of copper (Cu) and copper hydroxide (Cu(OH)2) to later be observed by SEM confirming the star morphology, meanwhile for the EDS analysis significant changes were observed in the composition of the manufactured nanostars, finally the samples were evaluated by SERS measurements using methylene blue (MB) detecting a aqueous solution with a concentration of 1x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>M.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Mechanical Properties In Fiber-Reinforced Epoxy Composites With Luffa Aegyptiaca
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This study explores the mechanical and chemical properties of Luffa aegyptiaca fiber reinforced epoxy composites, enhanced through various chemical treatments. Luffa aegyptiaca fibers, both in particulate and short forms, were subjected to treatments using NaOH, benzoyl chloride, and phenyltriethoxysilane to modify their surface chemistry and topography, as evidenced by Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) analyses. The mechanical properties, including tensile and flexural strength, alongside water absorption capabilities and chemical resistance, were evaluated for both treated and untreated fibers. Results demonstrated significant improvements in mechanical strengths and chemical resistance in treated fibers compared to their untreated counterparts, with saline treated particulate fiber composites showing the most substantial enhancements. These findings suggest that treated Luffa aegyptiaca fiber composites could serve as viable materials for applications such as furniture and construction components, providing a sustainable alternative to conventional synthetic composites.

articleTitle: Magnetic sensors with application in lithium ion batteries (LIBs)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are currently the fastest growing devices in the international battery market and the preferred energy storage system for applications in industries, including power systems for sustainable vehicles such as hybrid and electric vehicles, electric aircraft, small and medium-sized electronic devices and smart healthcare [1]. Magnetism is one of the forces that can be used to improve performance, since the use of magnetic fields influences electrochemical reactions through the variation of the properties of the electrolyte, as well as mass conduction, kinetics of the electrodes, among others [2]. LIBs have been widely applied in a variety of industries, including smart healthcare, small and medium-sized electronic devices, to name a few [3]. In this article we will talk about the characteristics that magnetic sensors must have such as sensitivity, dynamic range, stability, among others. It will explore using different sensor technologies. The objective of this article is to present the different types of magnetic sensors for the direct and non-invasive reading of the magnetic field of Li-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Designing a mockup and refactoring code for HPC geo-electromagnetic applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive integration of object-oriented code refactoring within PETGEM, an open-source 3D electromagnetic modeler, aimed at advancing its functionality for geophysical applications in the exascale high-performance computing era. Building upon previous works focusing on PETGEM, our research extends the capabilities of PETGEM by enhancing its codebase organization, design extensibility, and computational efficiency through its integration with the PETSc library. To achieve this goal, we first introduce a mockup design based on PETSc to emulate the PETGEM workflow. Subsequently, we utilize this mockup to implement object-oriented code refactoring techniques. The net result of this effort is an improved code version and better interoperability, portability, and scalability for the solution of real-life geo-electromagnetic surveys in geophysics.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic controller for a terrestrial mobile robot based on the global positioning system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The main challenge in mobile robotics is navigation, especially in autonomous navigation, where environmental uncertainty plays a crucial role in the robot’s ability to locate and move effectively in space. One of the most common sensors employed in this task is the Global Positioning System (GPS), which allows determining the position of an object at any point on Earth. However, using a low-cost GPS presents limitations regarding location accuracy, further complicating the problem of autonomous navigation. In this context, this paper proposes a methodology based on a fuzzy controller that uses the data provided by a low-cost GPS to guide the robot toward a preloaded destination point. This fuzzy controller is composed of five rules, and in the defuzzification stage, one-to-one relationships are employed, simplifying the decision-making process. As a result of the implementation of this methodology, a navigation precision with an error of less than 0.5 meters was achieved, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed fuzzy controller in autonomous navigation scenarios with low-cost sensors.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Results in the Determination of the Ambiental Thermal Sensation in an Area of the Gulf of Mexico during Solar Cycle 23 based on Daily Data and Monthly Average Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The Environmental Thermal Sensation (STA) in solar cycle 23 was determined from the daily data and the monthly data of the meteorological variables Temperature (T), Relative Humidity (H) and Wind Speed (VV), this calculation is performed using algorithms used by weather stations around the world. Being able to select a database that provides the most accurate information is essential to achieve the most accurate results that allow finding viable solutions for present and future decision-making. Therefore, a mathematical representation of the calculations performed is presented, which allows determining that the use of daily data validates all the generated equations, contrary to the monthly data, which eliminates all the equations in which the variable H appears. This comparative study allows us to find a change in the p-value of the variable H depending on the type of data used, presenting p-values > 0.05 with the use of monthly average data and a p-value < 0.05 with daily data. The best result of the resulting equation, with monthly average data of the combination of the variables T, H and VV presents a correlation coefficient of 0.999638 and a determination coefficient of 0.999261, but the variable H presents a p-value > 0.05, which rules it out, however, this same combination of variables with daily data gives a correlation coefficient of 0.997600 and a determination coefficient of 0.995203. The selection of daily data or monthly average data is definitive in the desired result to determine the Environmental Thermal Sensation of solar cycle 23 in the Veracruz-Boca del Rio Conurbation Zone. This research is in line with SDG 13 in the framework of the scientific need to know a problem from the root, allowing from the results obtained, to have a clarity in the use of scientific information necessary for the development of new strategies for the study of climate change.

articleTitle: Assessment of Thermal and Physico-Mechanical Properties in Recycled LDPE Composite Reinforced with Prosopis africana Wood Powder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Investigations were conducted into the thermal and physico-mechanical properties of recycled low-density polyethylene composites reinforced with Prosopis africana (PA). Compression molding equipment and a Two-Roll Mill were used to compound the constituents. Using standard methods, properties such as density, water absorption, tensile strength, elastic modulus, flexural strength, and hardness values were assessed. The materials were additionally put through a dynamic mechanical property test to determine how the inclusion of PA fiber affected the damping parameter, storage modulus, and loss modulus of recycled low-density polyethylene (rLDPE). Maximum flexural strength of 68.8 MPa, stiffness of 2.05 GPa, hardness of 70 Shores, and tensile strength of 58.5 MPa with a 20% weight proportion of reinforcement.In a similar vein, the results of the dynamic mechanical characteristics showed that the greatest load bearing capacity and storage modulus (1.2 GPa) for a composite containing 20% PA fiber were found (compared to 400 MPa of the unreinforced), however, as temperature and frequency increased, a drop in loss modulus was noted. This indicates that incorporation of PA fibre into rLDPE improved its physical, mechanical and dynamic mechanical properties

articleTitle: PDFL+I Control for the Pendu-copter stabilization: Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this paper we present a control strategy to stabilize the mechatronic system propeller driven pendulum or Pendu-copter. In base of the classical PID control, we combine this controller with a Fuzzy Logic (FL) Controller, using the proportional derivative action in the inference machine to have a faster convergence time and the integral action let to the system arrive to the desired stationary state in a finite time. The results are presented using numerical simulations as well as experimental tests, showing the good performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Investigation of Graphene Field-Effect Transistor Behavior Using a Semiclassical Transport Model and Monte Carlo Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional silicon transistors due to the exceptional electronic properties of graphene. In this work, we present a detailed study of GFET modeling and simulation using the Monte Carlo method. Our objective is to develop a semiclassical transport model based on the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) and perform simulations to study the transport characteristics and performance of GFETs under different operating conditions, considering the main scattering mechanisms in graphene. To carry out the simulations, we have developed our own Monte Carlo program in Octave, which allows us to have full control over the model parameters and adapt the simulations to our specific needs. Using this program, we study the influence of different device parameters, such as channel length and width and impurity concentration, in the electron distribution, carrier trajectories, and current-voltage characteristics of GFET, among other aspects. Our results reveal that the electron distribution becomes more uniform as the gate voltage increases, indicating a higher concentration of carriers in the channel. We observe ballistic behavior of carriers in the graphene channel, with limited scattering. Likewise, we observe a quasi-ballistic behavior of the carriers in the graphene channel, with limited dispersion.

articleTitle: Fundamentals of nonlinear sliding velocity in microchannels under non-Newtonian regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This research compiles knowledge essential for correct understanding of microscale electroosmotic flow phenomena under nonlinear hydrophobic sliding conditions. It begins with the definition of microfluidics, the branch of science from which the study of electrokinetic phenomena is derived and continues with key concepts for electroosmosis such as the theoretical characterization of the electric dual layer. Next, electrokinetic event occurring on hydrophobic surfaces are studied and the principles governing the characteristic equations of microchannel flow are established, as well as the boundary conditions that delimit it. Finally, the latest theoretical and scientific advances regarding microchannel fluid flow under the influence of electroosmotic phenomena and wall slip phenomena are compiled, with special emphasis on non-Newtonian fluids and nonlinear slip.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Organic Photodetectors with Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In Photodetectors applied to next generation biomedicine need to be flexible and stretchable to adapt to the human body. Commercial photodetectors are made of inorganic with poor mechanical flexibility. On the contrary, the polymer and small molecule photodetectors have appeared as favorable options for their mechanical properties, procedure, and biocompatibility. This article summarizes the current progress in photodetectors with organic materials in their optoelectronic advances and highlights their use in portable electronics for health monitoring.

articleTitle: Techniques of SAST Tools in the Early Stages of Secure Software Development: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Code analysis is an activity that requires multiple resources, especially when seeking to identify vulnerabilities that compromise the integrity of the software, as it necessitates specialized personnel. Even with this, a considerable amount of time is required to cover all the code. Static application security testing (SAST) tools allow for the analysis of source code without needing a compiled version through static analysis. This work presents an introduction to SAST tools and various techniques, such as static code-level analysis, syntactic analysis, code scanning, code similarity, pattern similarity, and taint analysis. It describes the generic functioning of SAST tools, which transform the source code into a comprehensible model for the tool, then use analysis algorithms to finally generate a report of results. The integration of SAST tools in the early stages of software development is analyzed, leveraging their automation and integration with version control, as well as compatibility with multiple programming languages for greater coverage. This research also addresses the limitations encountered when using SAST tools, such as the high rate of false positives and limited coverage, which requires the use of multiple tools for acceptable vulnerability detection. However, it highlights the importance of early vulnerability detection and the automation of the code analysis process, providing quick and efficient mechanisms.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Study of cylindrical WECS on the coasts of the Gulf of Mexico
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: SummaryThe present study is a hydrodynamic analysis of various vertical cylinder-type wave energy converter devices (WEC), covering the design part of the cylinder, hydrodynamic response analysis in HydroD, and coupled analysis in DeepC. Configurations with the best hydrodynamic performance for the WEC were tested. The design stage of the energy converters was an iterative process, and it was decided to place the tanks at the bottom of the structures as in the design of the platforms type SPARs. Seven energy converter devices were selected to analyze: WEC (diameter)x(draft) with diameters from 2 meters to 6 meters and drafts from 4 to 12 meters. The obtained results made it possible to identify the cylinders that present the most dynamics and their corresponding wave period. The influence of the mooring system was also recognized, and how it can contribute to controlling the movements of the cylinder so that it can produce electrical energy efficiently towards the final design.

articleTitle: Neutral-Point Voltage Interactions on a Medium-Voltage DC-Link
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The neutral-point-clamped (NPC) converter has been often used in power systems for various applications. A key difficulty with its application is the balancing of the neutral-point (NP) voltage. If this is not done correctly then harmonics can appear at the output voltage and overvoltages can cause device failure. Much research has been carried out to balance the NP voltage. However, investigations have mainly focused on single converters, without considering the interactions of the NP voltages of various connected NPC converters. Research has rarely examined the NP voltages under dynamic conditions. Herein, we present the study of the interaction of NP voltages of two converters connected via a medium-voltage DC (MVDC)-link. In addition, we examine the relationships between the NP voltages and the operation of the converters. Our results may help to improve the implementation of NPC converters to increasingly complex power systems. This will enable the connection of renewable energy sources and distributed generation, which require specific considerations of robustness and stability.
